title: The Milky Way’s big sister
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 6744, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 6744 · constellation Pavo · about 35 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Hubble's view of the spiral galaxy NGC 6744 shows a bright central region packed with old yellow stars. Farther out, dusty spiral arms appear in shades of pink and blue. The blue patches are full of young star clusters, while the pink ones mark regions where stars are actively forming, a sign that the galaxy is still very lively.

At first glance NGC 6744 looks like our own Milky Way, only bigger. It measures more than 200 000 light-years across, compared with about 100 000 light-years for our galaxy. The resemblance goes beyond size: like the Milky Way, it has a prominent core crowded with old stars.

More evidence of activity came in 2005, when a supernova named SN 2005at was discovered in the galaxy, though it does not appear in this image. It was a Type Ic supernova, which forms when a massive star collapses in on itself and loses its envelope of hydrogen.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.69 x 2.70 arcminutes) and distance (35 million light years), the frame spans roughly 27,000 × 27,000 light-years. Its light set out about 35 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes mainly from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, with an older Hubble camera adding hydrogen-alpha data, across ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared filters. The colours assigned to each filter are not published.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, and Hubble's long exposures show far more detail than an eye at a telescope could.

explore: NGC 6744 lies about 35 million light-years away, in the southern constellation of Pavo. The picture combines observations in ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared light, including a filter that picks out the glow of hydrogen gas.
alt: A large spiral galaxy with a yellowish core and dusty arms dotted with pink and blue patches.
